<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

The NPU precise-test recommend job needs a fresh coverage baseline
(`outputs.tar.gz` + `test_case_map.json`) in Huawei OBS, which it downloads over
anonymous HTTPS to pick which tests to run. Today that baseline has to be
uploaded by hand after every run, so it drifts stale, and each step of the
pipeline has its own gaps:

- **Retries lose coverage.** `Re-run failed jobs` only re-executes the failed
  jobs, so a new attempt dir holds just a subset of the tests. Merging only the
  current attempt produces an incomplete report.
- **The gate and the displayed number can disagree.** The NPU-only percentage
  was computed inline while rendering `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which may be unset
  on the k8s runner pool, so no persisted value existed for a threshold check.
- **The baseline was never gated.** A run with little or no coverage data could
  overwrite a good baseline in OBS.
- **Unowned run dirs accumulate.** Per-attempt dirs were cleaned up only when
  the publish step succeeded, so failures left them behind indefinitely.
- **Too little PR-time NPU coverage.** Several NPU tests were registered
  nightly-only, so PR runs collected almost nothing to build the baseline from.

## Modifications

### `.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`

- Merge all attempts of the current run into a single run dir (`<run_id>-attempt-*`),
  newest first with the current attempt winning, so a re-run keeps coverage from
  the jobs it did not re-execute.
- Fold per-attempt date dirs (`outputs/sglang@<date>`) into one destination to
  handle attempts that cross midnight UTC and split across two date tags.
- Compute the NPU-only total once and persist it to `${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt`;
  the run-page summary and the OBS gate both read that value, so the gated and
  displayed numbers cannot diverge.
- Add an **Upload baseline to OBS** step that installs `obsutil` on demand and
  uploads `outputs.tar.gz` and `test_case_map.json` with `-acl=public-read`,
  then verifies an anonymous HTTPS `HEAD` returns 200 (a stale private ACL would
  otherwise only show up as a confusing failure in the next run).
- Gate the upload on NPU-only coverage >= 10%, failing closed when the value is
  missing; skip with a warning when there is no coverage data or the OBS secrets
  are unset, so a partial run never overwrites a good baseline.
- Let **Publish outputs and map to shared disk** run with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`
  — the shared-disk baseline is the primary product and must not be blocked by
  an OBS failure.
- Cleanup now removes every attempt dir of the current run and sweeps
  `*-attempt-*` dirs older than 480 min (above the 6h job limit, so a live run can
  never match), while keeping the shared `coverage/` dir out of reach.

### Test registrations

- `test_npu_glm5_top64_pruned_bf16_8p_gsm8k.py`: also register in
  `base-c-test-acc-16-npu-a3`.
- `test_npu_return_indexer_topk_deepseek_v4.py` and
  `test_npu_return_indexer_topk_glm52.py`: also register in
  `base-b-test-2-npu-a3`.

Nightly registration is unchanged; these tests now also run in PR CI, which both
widens PR-time coverage and feeds real data into the baseline.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -866,14 +866,48 @@ jobs:
           name: coverage-outputs-base-a-test-npu
           path: /tmp/base-a-coverage
 
-      - name: Merge base-a coverage into shared run dir
+      - name: Merge base-a coverage and earlier attempts into shared run dir
+        shell: bash
         run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
           # Artifact stages {RUN_DIR}/outputs/... — merges 1:1 into the shared layout.
           CACHE_ROOT="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test"
           mkdir -p "${CACHE_ROOT}"
           cp -a /tmp/base-a-coverage/. "${CACHE_ROOT}/"
           echo "Merged base-a coverage into ${CACHE_ROOT}:"
-          find "${CACHE_ROOT}" -maxdepth 3 -type d | head -20
+          find "${CACHE_ROOT}" -maxdepth 3 -type d | head -20 || true
+
+          # Re-run only re-executes failed jobs; union all attempts of this run
+          # (newest first, current attempt wins) so the report stays complete.
+          RUN_ID="${{ github.run_id }}"
+          CURRENT="${RUN_ID}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
+          # Date tag derivation must match run_tests_with_coverage.sh.
+          COV_DATE_TAG="${GITHUB_RUN_STARTED_AT:-$(date +%Y%m%d)}"
+          COV_DATE_TAG="${COV_DATE_TAG:0:10}"
+          COV_DATE_TAG="${COV_DATE_TAG//-/}"
+          DEST="${CACHE_ROOT}/${CURRENT}/outputs/sglang@${COV_DATE_TAG}"
+          mkdir -p "${DEST}"
+
+          # A single attempt can end up with two date dirs: when the runner
+          # falls back to `date` and the attempt crosses midnight UTC, jobs
+          # started on either side write under different tags. Fold them in,
+          # otherwise everything outside DEST's tag is dropped downstream.
+          for td in "${CACHE_ROOT}/${CURRENT}/outputs/sglang@"*/*; do
+            [ -d "${td}" ] || continue
+            [ -e "${DEST}/${td##*/}" ] || cp -a "${td}" "${DEST}/"
+          done
+
+          find "${CACHE_ROOT}" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d \
+            -name "${RUN_ID}-attempt-*" ! -name "${CURRENT}" -print0 \
+            | sort -zrV \
+            | while IFS= read -r -d '' prev; do
+                for td in "${prev}/outputs/sglang@"*/*; do
+                  [ -d "${td}" ] || continue
+                  [ -e "${DEST}/${td##*/}" ] || cp -a "${td}" "${DEST}/"
+                done
+              done
+          echo "Test dirs in ${DEST}: $(find "${DEST}" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d | wc -l)"
 
       - name: Copy sglang source to covstub
         run: |
@@ -1147,7 +1181,7 @@ jobs:
           # The percentage is computed once by the "Generate HTML coverage
           # report" step above (same container). Fail closed when the value is
           # missing, e.g. that step died before writing it.
-          MIN_NPU_COVERAGE=40
+          MIN_NPU_COVERAGE=10
           NPU_PCT_FILE="${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt"
           if [ ! -s "${NPU_PCT_FILE}" ]; then
             echo "::error::NPU-only coverage value missing (${NPU_PCT_FILE}); refusing to upload the baseline to OBS"
@@ -1258,21 +1292,18 @@ jobs:
           ls -lh "${PUBLISH_DIR}" | tail -n +2
 
       - name: Clean up per-run directory
-        # Default success() on purpose: any earlier failure (incl. the OBS
-        # upload) keeps RUN_DIR for manual recovery.
-        # A successful run also sweeps leftovers from earlier failed runs, so
-        # residue does not pile up. Only dirs older than STALE_MINUTES: RUN_DIR
-        # is per-run for a reason, and a bare glob would delete the directory
-        # of a concurrently running job mid-flight.
+        # success() by default: earlier failures keep the run dirs for debugging.
+        # Attempts never overlap and earlier ones are already merged, so drop
+        # all of this run's attempt dirs at once; stale ones from old runs go too.
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           CACHE_ROOT="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test"
-          RUN_DIR="${CACHE_ROOT}/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
+          RUN_PREFIX="${CACHE_ROOT}/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-"
           # 8h > the 6h per-job execution limit, so a live run can never match.
           STALE_MINUTES=480
-          rm -rf "${RUN_DIR}"
-          echo "Removed ${RUN_DIR}"
+          rm -rf "${RUN_PREFIX}"*
+          echo "Removed ${RUN_PREFIX}*"
           # -maxdepth 1 keeps the shared coverage/ dir out of reach.
           find "${CACHE_ROOT}" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d \
             -name '*-attempt-*' -mmin +"${STALE_MINUTES}" \

@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@
 from sglang.utils import wait_for_server
 
 register_npu_ci(est_time=400, suite="nightly-2-npu-a3", nightly=True)
+register_npu_ci(est_time=400, suite="base-b-test-2-npu-a3")
